name: UIBlurSource
src_typeComment: Drop on the MAIN CAMERA (whatever camera renders the 3D/2D scene the UI sits over) to capture and blur its view into ONE shared, deliberately LOW-RESOLUTION RenderTexture, published via Shader.SetGlobalTexture — every Toolkit/UI/Glass Blur material samples the exact same texture automatically, no per-element wiring needed. This is the whole point versus GrabPass: one controlled, low-res copy shared by every glass element per frame, not a fresh full-resolution screen copy per object (see the GrabPass explanation this tool was built after).  Captured via a SEPARATE camera on OnPostRender, not the actual player camera's own output — this keeps the capture from ever including the UI Canvas itself (Screen Space Overlay UI renders after and outside normal camera rendering entirely, so it's naturally excluded; a Screen Space Camera canvas assigned to THIS SAME camera would need its own render layer excluded from `reflectionMask`-style filtering, which isn't set up here since the toolkit's own demo — and the common case — uses Overlay).

src_serialized.name: resolutionScale
src_serialized.tooltip: Capture resolution as a fraction of the screen. Quarter (0.25) is the deliberate default — blur wants low resolution anyway, and this is the actual cost lever.

src_serialized.name: blurPasses
src_serialized.tooltip: Box-blur passes to apply. Repeated box blur cheaply approximates a Gaussian blur — more passes = smoother/blurrier, more cost.

src_serialized.name: blurSpread
src_serialized.tooltip: Blur sample spread, in texels of the LOW-RES capture. Larger spreads the blur wider per pass.

src_serialized.name: captureEveryNFrames
src_serialized.tooltip: Re-captures every N frames instead of every frame — the background behind glass rarely needs to be perfectly current.

src_members.name: ForceCapture
src_members.comment: Public so it can be triggered outside the normal per-frame OnPostRender schedule — a self-test driving it directly (OnPostRender never fires outside an actual camera render pass, which batch mode doesn't perform), or a game explicitly wanting one fresh capture right before opening a menu.
